description:
Cron HEARTBEAT that (re)starts the singleton drain-until-caught-up embedder for the LED-01 event-content search index. Each fire does ZERO embedding on the action-queue thread: it submits ONE background drainer to a single-slot executor and returns in milliseconds with `{"drainer": "started", "page_size": N}`, or `{"drainer": "already_running", ...}` if a drainer is already active (that fire is a no-op). At most one drainer runs at a time PER PROCESS — a dedicated in-memory executor slot (separate from the auto-summarize slot, so the two drains run independently) is the singleton guard.

The drainer (`EventEmbeddingWriter.drain_missing_events`) walks a DURABLE cursor forward in ARRIVAL order — keyed on `imported_at` (platform receive time, per-row `now()` at append, index `idx_event_imported_at`), NOT vendor `event_at`. This is load-bearing: `event_at` is vendor wall-clock, so a historical session imported AFTER the cursor advanced (a cloud/export/history backfill — the ledger's routine load) carries an OLD `event_at`, and an `event_at` frontier would strand it in a permanent silent gap; a newly imported historical event carries a fresh arrival timestamp and is caught; the periodic full reconciliation covers commit-visibility races. Each page it reads `list_event_embedding_candidates` (default `page_size` 100, clamped to the read's 1..100 cap; ordered `imported_at, id` ascending) — the SQL scope legs (`event_type = MESSAGE`, `role` in user/assistant, `content_text` not null) plus the Python leg (the Codex `reasoning` subtype exclusion) — asks the vector store which chunk-0 external_ids are missing, embeds those events via the LOCAL embedding model (no inference — nomic locally, titan on cloud), and advances + PERSISTS the cursor (a single `imported_at` timestamp) to the page's last row. The cursor is a single GLOBAL key-value row (`session_ledger`/`event_embed_cursor`); the drain restarts INCLUSIVELY at it (an empty-string id sentinel that sorts before every uuid) so same-arrival ties re-surface and are `find_missing`-skipped.

Four properties. O(N) BACKFILL, O(new) STEADY STATE: a caught-up fire reads only arrivals past the cursor, not a full-corpus rescan every fire. RECONCILIATION (hard completeness): every Nth fire IGNORES the cursor and re-checks the whole corpus — `imported_at` is assigned in Python BEFORE the autocommit insert, so it is not commit-visibility-monotonic and a row can commit into visibility BELOW the advanced cursor; the periodic full `find_missing` sweep re-reads and embeds it, making completeness a hard EVENTUAL guarantee (bounded by one reconcile interval), not probabilistic. RESTART-RESUMABLE: a full policy/reconciliation sweep persists its composite completed-page cursor separately from the normal arrival frontier and resumes it after restart or service outage, without regressing normal progress. Clean completion records the target policy before retiring the checkpoint. MISSING WORK ONLY: unreadable sweep progress loses where a sweep was, not the vectors; the fresh sweep compares against the recorded chunk policy and embeds only missing or policy-changed chunks, and a running generation still carrying the legacy previous policy `unknown:corrupt` is corrected in place to the recorded policy with its progress kept (prb_f6964132: that marker made every event stale, so the sweep re-embedded the whole corpus). Under a backfill from a reproducible policy, an event whose new-policy chunk ids already exist is skipped as current (`events_skipped_current`), and no event is embedded twice in one fire. NEW ARRIVALS FIRST: while a sweep is running, each fire first drains arrivals past the cursor, then resumes the sweep, so new conversation content does not wait behind a corpus re-walk. BOUNDED DUTY CYCLE: CPU inference would otherwise run back to back on one core, so after every embedded event and every page the drain sleeps worked*(1-duty)/duty. The busy duty `SOLET_EVENT_EMBED_BUSY_DUTY` (default 0.1, about a tenth of one core on average) applies while the ledger is receiving new in-scope arrivals; the idle duty `SOLET_EVENT_EMBED_IDLE_DUTY` (default 1.0, full speed) applies only once the newest arrival is older than `SOLET_EVENT_EMBED_IDLE_AFTER_SECONDS` (default 900). Settings are read at the start of each fire; an invalid value or a failed idle read uses the busy duty and logs an advisory. Each fire reports `paused_ms`. Page-start and page-complete INFO logs report page, cursor, embedded/failed/deferred totals and sweep/pending state without content. Terminal results/logs report pending checkpoint and next reconciliation timing. TRANSIENT-SAFE / POISON-LOUD: generation outages, delete/store failures and unknown errors defer the page without advancing progress; only generation/input failures followed by a successful generation probe are skipped as isolated refusals, the fire halts (`halted_on_error` true) and the next heartbeat retries the same page once the embedder recovers (idempotent delete-before-store + skip-existing means no double work). One event that fails while the embedder still works is skipped with a WARNING naming its event_id and counted in `events_failed`, so it cannot stall the cursor for its page; it stays un-embedded, a sweep that skipped an event retains its original previous policy and an exhausted-with-failures checkpoint in existing session_ledger KV; ordinary fires continue incrementally and only the existing 144-fire reconciliation reopens a full retry, and the periodic reconciliation sweep retries it, so the gap is never silent. A re-embed hard-deletes the event's old chunk ids first (the vector table's `external_id` is unique, so a soft-deleted tombstone would block the replacement).

This is the LED-01 steady-state that mirrors `summarize_quiescent_sessions` for the EVENT corpus (operator directive: embedding runs automatically, the same manner as auto-summarize) — cron-fired via `ensure_periodic_embed_schedule`, the whole historical backlog fills in the background with no operator loop.

EDGE_SINK (terminal/headless) — no `result_processor_customizations` / `error_processor_customizations`; the cron-fired action short-circuits at the EDGE_SINK_SKIP branch in `action_queue_poller`. See `21_scheduling_service/01_template_flow_record_lifecycle.md` for the terminal-cron pattern.
embedding_description: Cron heartbeat starting the singleton event-content drain. Uses arrival-order incremental progress and resumable policy-sweep checkpoints. Store/delete/unknown outages defer pages; isolated generation refusals remain pending for the existing 144-fire reconciliation retry. Page progress and terminal logs expose pending work.
